item.title: HDFC Bank’s Bonds Fall to Record Low After CEO’s Shock Exit
item.description: Newly issued dollar bonds by HDFC Bank Ltd., India’s most valuable lender, slid to record lows on Tuesday as Chief Executive Officer Sashidhar Jagdishan’s unexpected decision to step down continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

item.title: Modi Urges Indians to Curb Gold Buying in Self-Reliance Push
item.description: Indians should avoid buying gold unless necessary, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, renewing an appeal to curb bullion demand as a widening trade deficit and weaker rupee strain the economy.

item.title: Payout by Top Africa Grocer Shoprite Beats as It Buys Vida Chain
item.description: Shoprite Holdings Ltd.’s dividend beat estimates as profit rose, with Africa’s biggest grocer buying the Vida e Caffè coffee-shop chain and a majority stake in R&A Cellular to give it more exposure to quick-service restaurants as well as the technology and payments space.

item.title: India Rupee at Two-Month High as Central Bank Supports Currency
item.description: India’s rupee strengthened to a two-month high as the central bank, bolstered by record foreign-exchange reserves, stepped in to support the local currency through dollar sales.

item.title: Ather Energy’s 130% Stock Surge Leaves Tesla, BYD Behind in 2026
item.description: India’s electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy Ltd. is beating global EV stocks this year, with analysts pointing to more gains on its growing market share.

item.title: Veritas Capital to Buy UK’s Bodycote for £1.65 Billion
item.description: Veritas Capital agreed to buy Bodycote Plc for around £1.65 billion ($2.2 billion), after raising its bid to trump CVC Advisers Ltd.

item.title: Epiris Agrees to Buy Gamma Communications for £1 Billion
item.description: Private equity firm Epiris has agreed to buy Gamma Communications Plc for about £1 billion ($1.4 billion), following a months-long takeover saga for the European enterprise communications provider.

item.title: France’s 2027 Election Is Already Placing Assets Under Pressure
item.description: Even eight months out from France’s presidential election, the country’s assets are already starting to show signs of pressure.

item.title: Jollibee Picks Hong Kong Over US for International Unit Listing
item.description: Philippine fast-food giant Jollibee Foods Corp. is pivoting to a Hong Kong listing for its international unit, abandoning an earlier plan to sell shares in the US.

item.title: UK House Prices Edged Back Up in August, Nationwide Says
item.description: UK house prices rose in August according to one of the country’s top mortgage lenders, suggesting that demand is holding up despite the economic effects of ongoing conflict between the US and Iran.

item.title: RBI’s Short Dollar Book Surges to Record on Diaspora Deposits
item.description: The RBI’s net short dollar book jumped to a record $136.8 billion in July, reflecting rising future obligations from its measures to lure foreign capital, including a special deposit program for overseas Indians.

item.title: Mozambican President Appoints De Sousa as Central Bank Governor
item.description: Mozambican President Appoints De Sousa as Central Bank Governor【原文：Mozambican President Appoints De Sousa as Central Bank Governor】

item.title: India’s Growth Beat Suggests Economy on Cusp of Investment Boom
item.description: India’s long-awaited private investment cycle may finally be stirring, adding another engine of growth that could help the world’s fastest-growing major economy sustain its momentum after years of heavy lifting by the government.

item.title: Japan’s 10-Year Bond Yield Hits 3% for First Time Since 1996
item.description: Japan’s 10-year government bond yield touched 3% for the first time this century, an important milestone for a debt market that is returning to normality after benchmark borrowing costs languished near zero for years.

item.title: Korea Plans Near-Record Bond Issuance to Fund 2027 Spending
item.description: South Korea plans to issue a near-record 222.8 trillion won ($162.7 billion) of bonds in 2027 as President Lee Jae Myung pushes his expansionary fiscal agenda.

item.title: Chip Tax Windfall Spurs South Korea’s Record Budget Expansion
item.description: South Korea is planning a record expansion in state spending next year to finance an artificial-intelligence investment drive, while channeling more than 160 trillion won ($117 billion) of a semiconductor-fueled tax windfall into a new fund.

item.title: Japan’s Finance Chief Plays Down Bessent’s BOJ Rate Hike Push
item.description: Japan’s Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said that she and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent share the view that their recent joint intervention in the currency market was beneficial, while playing down reports that he has been pushing for the Bank of Japan to raise its policy rate.

item.title: Global Bond Selloff Sends Yields to the Highest Level Since 2008
item.description: Global bond yields climbed back to the highest level in almost two decades as rising oil prices fueled inflation concerns and investors ramped up expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates.

item.title: Chinese Manufacturing Gauge Clocks Longest Upswing in Five Years
item.description: China’s factory activity expanded more than forecast in August after three straight months of slowdown, according to a private survey, showing resilience among the country’s export-oriented firms despite a broader slowdown in the economy.

item.title: Japan Ministries Seek Record Budget as Yields Hit 30-Year High
item.description: Japan’s ministries requested a record amount of spending for next fiscal year, putting Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s fiscal ambitions in sharper focus as the yield on benchmark government bonds touched 3% for the first time in three decades.

item.title: US 30-Year Bond Enters September on Worst Stretch Since 2006
item.description: Not since 2006 have yields on the longest-maturity Treasuries been this high for this long, with a gaping budget deficit, another wave of corporate issuance and a potentially decisive Federal Reserve meeting set to keep investors wary of US debt in coming weeks.

item.title: Nvidia Mega-Deal Ushers MediaTek Into Top AI Chipmaker Club
item.description: Nvidia Corp.’s $3.5 billion outlay in MediaTek Inc., its largest direct investment outside the US, has thrust a little-known Taiwanese chip designer into the center of the global AI infrastructure boom.

item.title: Japan’s Companies Boost Capital Investment as Profits Surge
item.description: Japanese companies raised capital spending in the second quarter as profits surged, in the latest sign that the corporate sector is coping fairly well with the fallout from the Middle East conflict.

item.title: South Korea’s Exports Gather Pace as Chip Boom Powers Ahead
item.description: South Korea’s exports extended their strong growth in August as artificial-intelligence demand powered chip shipments and the broader economy, giving the central bank little reason to retreat from its newly hawkish stance after back-to-back interest-rate hikes.

item.title: Gold Holds Decline as Mideast Flare-Up Raises Fed Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: Gold steadied after a two-day drop as the US and Iran exchanged strikes for the first time in a month, raising the odds of rising energy costs pushing up inflation and pressuring the Federal Reserve to lift interest rates.

item.title: Anthropic Seals $35 Billion Cloud Deal With Nvidia-Backed Lambda
item.description: Anthropic PBC agreed to a $35 billion computing deal with Lambda, a cloud provider backed by Nvidia Corp., part of an effort to quickly expand its AI capacity, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: Malaysia Bonds Lag Peers in August on Supply, Rate-Hike Concerns
item.description: Malaysian bonds delivered Southeast Asia’s worst performance in August as concern over the supply of long-dated notes and the risk of an interest-rate hike made investors cautious.

item.title: Australia’s Beetaloo Shale Gas Could Power Northern Territory AI Data Centers
item.description: Australia’s Northern Territory started commercial production from the nation’s first shale gas wells, as the sparsely populated region bets on the fossil fuel to power a wave of new data centers.

item.title: US Funds Alcoa Gallium Plant in Australia to Cut China Reliance
item.description: The US Department of War said it will provide $174 million in financing to Alcoa Corp. to build a gallium plant at its alumina refinery in Western Australia, as Washington seeks to reduce its reliance on China for critical minerals.
